name: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4

validation.notes: Built from launch-week research. HUD positions are configurable in the game and were not checked against live captures; the recogniser reads what it can and leaves the rest out.

capture.notes: Borderless windowed mode captures most reliably. For the death map, set the minimap to fixed (not rotating) in the game's HUD settings.

modes.label: Private match vs bots only (no other players)
Multiplayer (core, Ground War, Gunfight, party modes)

playerContext.label: Your usual primary weapon (optional)
playerContext.help: Helps the coach talk about ranges and engagements that suit your loadout.

playerContext.label: Your minimap
playerContext.help: With a fixed (north-up) minimap the coach stitches the map from it and pins where you die to the spot; with a rotating one, only to the area.

vision.purpose: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 (Multiplayer, DMZ or Campaign). Read the team scores and match timer if shown, the player's own kills and deaths only if shown (scoreboard or end-of-match screen), and what screen this is (lobby, loadout editor, map vote, loading, in match, killcam, scoreboard, after-action report). Detect when the player's own character dies (death screen, killcam of the player, respawn prompt) and, from the kill card or killfeed, what killed them. Detect the player's own kills only from a clear kill marker or a killfeed line with the player's name. The HUD can be moved (HUD bounds) and the minimap can be square or round, fixed or rotating; read what is there, guess nothing. On a killcam of the player's death, also read the fight: how exposed the player was, what they were doing, the range, who was higher, whether friendly dots were near on the death-screen minimap, and how many enemies engaged. Give unknown for anything not clearly visible.

state.label: Your team's score
state.description: The player's team score on the HUD or scoreboard. Omit if you cannot tell which side is the player's.

state.label: Time left (s)
state.description: The match timer converted to seconds, if shown.

state.label: Kills
state.description: The player's own kill count, only if shown (scoreboard, after-action report).

state.label: Deaths
state.description: The player's own death count, only if shown.

state.label: Current kill streak
state.description: The player's current streak counter on the scorestreak widget, if a number is shown.

state.label: Map
state.description: The map name, from a loading screen, map vote or scoreboard header.

state.label: Mode
state.description: The game mode name (e.g. Domination, Hardpoint), from a loading screen or scoreboard.

state.label: Your weapon
state.description: The name of the weapon the player is holding, as shown in the HUD's weapon panel (e.g. 'MCW', 'Holger 556'). Omit if not visible.

state.label: Enemy killstreaks
state.description: Killstreaks the enemy team called in, shown in this frame by the announcer text, killfeed icon or a warning (e.g. 'UAV, Cluster Strike'). Comma-separated names; omit if none.

state.label: Where you are
state.description: Where the player is right now, as one callout name from this map's list in the Game reference, judged from the player's OWN first-person view (buildings, signs, materials, objectives) and the minimap. Not on killcams, spectating or menus. Omit if unsure; never pick a name just to say something.

state.label: Your height
state.description: The player's own height layer right now: underground, ground, upper (an upper floor, balcony or raised walkway) or roof. Own view only; omit if unsure.

state.label: Killer's spot
state.description: On a killcam or death replay: the callout the killer shot from (from the killcam's view of their surroundings), from this map's list. Omit if not a killcam or unsure.

state.label: Killer's weapon
state.description: On the death screen or killcam: the killer's weapon name exactly as shown (use the Arsenal names). Omit otherwise.

state.label: Enemies seen
state.description: Callouts where enemies are visible right now (on screen, or as red pings on the minimap during a UAV), as 'count Callout', comma-separated, e.g. '2 Market, Clock Tower'. Never from the fog; omit if none.

events.label: You died
events.description: The player's own character is visibly dead in this frame: death screen, killcam showing the player being killed, or respawn prompt.

attributes.description: The weapon class or source that killed the player, from the kill card or killfeed.
Only from the killcam or a damage indicator: where the shot came from relative to where the player was looking.
From the killcam: how much of the player's body the killer could see. in_open = nothing between them; partial_cover = edge of cover or head glitch.
From the killcam: what the player was doing when the first shot landed. sprinting = gun lowered in a sprint pose; aiming_still = aiming down sights and not moving.
Distance between killer and player in the killcam: close under ~10 m, mid ~10-30 m, long beyond.
From the killcam, relative to the player: you_lower = the killer was clearly higher than the player; you_higher = the killer was clearly lower.
From the death screen minimap: a friendly dot within a short sprint of the player, or none. unknown if the minimap is not visible.
From the killcam or the HUD at death: reload animation or empty magazine, throwing equipment, firing, or not firing.
From the killcam or damage indicators: one enemy engaged the player, or two or more.

events.label: You got a kill
events.description: A kill marker (e.g. '+100' with an elimination) or a killfeed line naming the player as the killer.

attributes.description: Distance to the enemy the player just killed, from the frame: close under ~10 m, mid ~10-30 m, long beyond. unknown if the target is not visible.
What the player was doing at the kill, from their own view: scope up and still = aiming_still.
Relative to the player: you_higher = the player looks down at the enemy; you_lower = the player looks up at them.

events.label: Killstreak earned
events.description: A banner shows the player earned a killstreak.

zones.label: Minimap area
zones.description: Divide the visible minimap into a 3x3 grid as drawn on screen (top = north on a fixed minimap). Use the player's own arrow at the moment of death. If the minimap is not visible or is rotating, give no zone.

concepts.title: Reposition after a kill
concepts.summary: Staying in the same spot after a kill gives the enemy a known place to challenge. A short move to new cover after each fight resets the angle in your favour.
good: Move a few metres to new cover after a kill
Reload behind cover
bad: Holding the same angle after it was revealed
Reloading in the open

concepts.title: Use the minimap
concepts.summary: Red dots on the minimap and the UAV show where fights are. Glancing at it between fights avoids running into crossfires.
good: Check the minimap after every engagement
Move toward your team's side of a fight
bad: Running across open lanes the enemy controls

concepts.title: Fight at your weapon's range
concepts.summary: SMGs and shotguns win close; assault rifles mid; snipers and marksman rifles long. Choosing routes that keep fights at your range wins more of them.
good: Take routes that suit your loadout
bad: Challenging a sniper lane with an SMG

concepts.title: Play the objective
concepts.summary: Objective actions build your streak too (Smart Streaks) and win matches. Capturing and holding often matters more than chasing kills.
good: Capture and hold in Domination and Hardpoint
bad: Ignoring the objective while the score slips

prohibitedAdvice: Positions of enemies that are not visible on the player's own screen
Exploits, glitches, or anything against Activision's rules
Anything that automates input or aiming

terminology.pre-aim: aiming where an enemy will appear before they do
terminology.trade: killing the enemy who just killed a teammate

items.name: Game identity
items.detail: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, developed by Infinity Ward (Beenox PC support, Digital Legends Switch 2 port). Released Oct 23, 2026 on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, PC and Nintendo Switch 2; no PS4/Xbox One. Campaign set on the Korean Peninsula (a second Korean War).

items.name: Release waves
items.detail: Campaign early access Oct 16, DMZ Oct 20, full launch Oct 23, 2026. Open Beta ran Aug 28 - Sep 1, 2026 (with earlier beta weekends). Shipment added Oct 27, Possession LTM Oct 29, Infected Oct 30, Season 1 + Warzone integration Nov 6, 2026.

items.name: Pillars of MW4 multiplayer
items.detail: Grounded movement (no omnimovement), no hipfire bloom ('Ballistic Authority'), slower Beta-Weekend-2 TTK kept for launch, pick-3 perks (18), 17 killstreaks attached per loadout, Smart Streak meter that rewards objective play, Apex attachments at max weapon level.

items.name: Launch content size
items.detail: 33 weapons (8 AR, 5 SMG, 3 LMG, 2 shotgun, 3 marksman, 3 sniper, 4 pistol, 4 launcher, 1 melee), 18 perks, 17 killstreaks, 12 field upgrades, 9 tacticals, 11 lethals, 12 core 6v6 maps, Kill Block, 4 Gunfight maps, 3 Ground War maps, roughly 13 launch modes plus a movement training course.

items.name: Progression
items.detail: Player levels 1-55 unlock weapons, perks, equipment and streaks (Create-a-Class opens at level 4). Then 10 Prestiges and 1,000 Prestige Master levels. Each prestige you choose Classic (reset unlocks, +20% XP, permanent unlock token) or Regular (keep everything). Weapon Prestige also returns.

items.name: DMZ is part of MW4
items.detail: DMZ returns as MW4's extraction mode on the Hajin map, with its own 1-70 level track and Operator Prestige. Gear is kept only if you exfil; dying marks your operator Missing In Action.

items.name: Warzone tie-in
items.detail: Warzone integrates MW4 on Nov 6, 2026 (Season 1): Hajin joins Battle Royale (Verdansk stays), Zodiac joins Resurgence, MW4 weapons/operators/movement arrive and omnimovement goes away. Warzone on PS4/Xbox One shuts down that day.

items.name: Current patch state (as of Oct 28)
items.detail: Launch patch notes (official, Oct ~21-25) did a full weapon/attachment balance pass, buffed SMGs at close-mid range, added flinch/damage tuning to one-hit-kill weapons, and made Tac Sprint a Blood Rush perk feature. IW said more weapon tuning was being looked at for the following week; no named nerfs found yet.

items.name: Ranked Play status
items.detail: No MW4 Ranked Play date announced as of Oct 28, 2026, and it is not on the Season 1 (Nov 6) roadmap. Precedent (MW3 launched Nov 2023, Ranked Jan 2024) suggests weeks to months later. Ranks/ruleset unknown. [Unverified]

items.name: Competitive scene
items.detail: MW4 is the game for the 2027 Call of Duty League season. Pros used HAN 86, M4, VEL 46 and ISO Nightshade in day-1 kickoff events. The official CDL ruleset/GA restrictions were not found in research. [Unverified]

items.name: Reception of UI
items.detail: Reviewers (Destructoid, Windows Central, The Outer Haven) and CharlieINTEL describe a cleaner, faster UI: vertical menus return, plus a left-docked pop-out sidebar/'blade' menu for quick access to class creation in MP and DMZ.

items.name: How to read this reference
items.detail: Facts tagged [Unverified] come from a single third-party guide, beta-era data, or conflicting sources. TTK/RPM numbers are community-measured and can shift with patches. Callofduty.com could not be fetched directly; official details come via search snippets.

items.name: Release
items.detail: Released Oct 23, 2026 by Infinity Ward and Activision on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, PC and Nintendo Switch 2; announced May 2026.

items.name: Season 1
items.detail: Season 1 and the Warzone integration arrive Nov 6, 2026.

items.name: PC requirements
items.detail: TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot are required for online play (RICOCHET Anti-Cheat).

items.name: No Zombies
items.detail: Three modes: Campaign, Multiplayer and DMZ; there is no Zombies mode.

items.name: Team Deathmatch
items.detail: 6v6 respawn. Each kill scores a point; most kills at time or first to the limit wins. Hardcore variant exists. Score 100 kills (raised from 75 in beta). Time 10 minutes. Win: Trade kills in pairs; Stack UAVs and pre-aim spawns. Mistake: Solo pushing into three enemies.

items.name: Kill Confirmed
items.detail: 6v6 respawn. Kills drop dog tags; pick up enemy tags to score and teammates' tags to deny. Hardcore variant exists. Score 75 tags. Time 10 minutes. Win: Kill where tags can be collected; Collect then reset to cover. Mistake: Long-range kills with no tag pickup.

items.name: Domination
items.detail: 6v6 respawn. Capture and hold flags A, B and C for points over time; sides swap at half score. Flag captures and holds feed the Smart Streak meter. Hardcore variant exists. Score 200. Time No time limit (official listing: unlimited). Win: Hold two flags (usually yours + B); Rotate together to recapture. Mistake: Triple-capping and flipping spawns without control.

items.name: Hardpoint
items.detail: 6v6 respawn. One zone at a time scores only while held uncontested; the zone rotates in a fixed per-map order (every 60 s per guides). Holding feeds the Smart Streak meter. Hardcore variant exists. Score 250. Time Official listing reportedly shows 5 minutes (verify in game). Win: Rotate ~10 s before the hill moves; Play off the zone with sightlines. Mistake: Late rotations.

items.name: Search & Destroy
items.detail: Round-based, one life per round, no respawns. Attackers plant the bomb at A or B; defenders prevent or defuse. Eliminating the other team also wins. Sides swap. Hardcore variant exists. Oct 25: kill XP raised to 300; bo…. Score First to 6 rounds. Time 2 minutes per round. Win: Use utility before entering; Trade every first kill. Mistake: Solo peeking without trade support.

items.name: Free-for-All
items.detail: Everyone against everyone, respawn. The top three players win. Party size reported as 1 (official) or 1-4 (Game Rant). Score 30 kills. Time 10 minutes. Win: Play edges where fewer players converge; Avoid open middles. Mistake: Running through the center.

items.name: Inflation (new)
items.detail: 6v6 respawn, 10 minutes, no score limit: team holding the most cash at the end wins. Eliminating enemies collects their cash; carrying lots of cash past a threshold reveals you to both teams as a high-value target. Dying drops part of your cash. Overtime in the final minutes adds bigger multipliers. Protect your rich carriers; hunt revealed enemies.

items.name: Hijack (new)
items.detail: 6v6 round-based. One Data Spike in the middle: carry, throw or pass it to the enemy Comm Station and plant it to score over time, with a bonus if the upload completes. Rounds 4 minutes, score limit 300, sides swap between rounds. Planting the Spike feeds the streak meter. (One outlier source describes a moving package instead.)

items.name: Frontline
items.detail: 6v6 respawn. Each team spawns in its own fixed base with brief spawn invincibility; sides change when a team hits half the score limit. Kills outside the enemy base are worth more (per guides). Score 100. Time 10 minutes. Win: Hold the middle with sightlines. Mistake: Pushing into the enemy base (low value and spawn-protected enemies).

items.name: Collateral (new)
items.detail: Counter-Strike-style bomb mode: attack/defend two sites, 2-minute rounds, first to 6 round wins. No custom classes: start with pistol and $800, earn cash for kills, objectives and round wins, buy weapons/armor/perks/equipment/team UAV. No respawn, no health regen, no streaks except team UAV. Death loses gear but keeps cash. Team size reported as 6v6 or 5v5 (conflict).

items.name: Gunfight (2v2)
items.detail: Single-life rounds; every player gets the same randomly assigned loadout. Maps: Cafe, Library, NYC, Smuggler. If time runs out, an Overtime Flag appears: capture it or win on remaining health. Win by playing together, trading and using utility early.

items.name: Kill Block Gunfight (3v3 / 10v10)
items.detail: Gunfight on the modular Kill Block arena. Official: 50-second rounds, first to 6, single life, shared random loadouts, sides swap after round one, then layout and loadout change every two rounds; Overtime Flag decides ties. Re-read sightlines after each layout change.

items.name: Ground War: Combat Outpost
items.detail: Large-scale Domination-style mode. Capture Outposts for points and forward spawns; reinforce held Outposts to unlock team rewards (local UAV, JLTV airdrop, Light Tank at HQ). Player count 32v32 per official listing (24v…. Score 1,500. Time 20 minutes. Win: Reinforce held Outposts for rewards; Use vehicles to support captures. Mistake: Ignoring Outposts to chase kills.

items.name: Gun Game (party mode)
items.detail: Free-for-all ladder: each kill advances you to the next weapon; first to finish wins. Melee setback is series standard, not MW4-confirmed. In the Oct 27 weekly playlist. Score Finish the weapon ladder. Win: Avoid crowded areas with weak weapons. Mistake: Getting melee'd and losing progress (series rule).

items.name: Possession (LTM, Oct 29)
items.detail: Halloween limited-time mode announced for Oct 29. Reported idea: eliminating an opponent lets you take over their position and loadout. Full ruleset not published at time of research. [Unverified]

items.name: Infected (Oct 30)
items.detail: One player starts Infected; Survivors they kill join the Infected. Survivors win by lasting to time; Infected win by converting everyone. Exact timer not published. Win: Survivors: hold choke points together. Mistake: Survivors splitting up.

items.name: Shipment 24/7 / Shipment
items.detail: Shipment (tiny container map) added Oct 27. Widely used for camo/weapon XP farming. Whether a dedicated 24/7 playlist exists was disputed between sources. [Unverified]

items.name: Hardcore variants
items.detail: Hardcore versions of core modes (e.g. Domination, Hardpoint) are listed at launch: reduced HUD, much lower health, friendly fire. Coach note: minimap info is limited, so rely on sound and UAVs.

items.name: Counter Attack / Drop Zone
items.detail: Mentioned in older coverage and one modes site, but a GamerFuzion read of the official launch list says both are missing at launch. Treat as not available until seen in game. [Unverified]

items.name: Ranked Play
items.detail: Not live as of Oct 28, 2026; no official date (estimates Dec 2026 to early 2027; not on the Nov 6 Season 1 list). Expected to use the CDL ruleset (4v4, Hardpoint, S&D, a third mode, restricted items). CMG Arena banned k…. Win: Expect a restricted item list. Mistake: Assuming pub-style loadouts will be legal.

items.name: DMZ (Hajin)
items.detail: Extraction mode: squads (reported up to 3) deploy into Hajin, complete contracts, fight AI and players, then exfil by helicopter at Tac-Map exfil zones (calling it alerts nearby players/AI; stay aboard until the timer hits zero), Fulton balloons or Exfil Flares. Die and you lose carried gear. Killing 4 operators makes you Wanted. Separate 1-70 level track.

items.name: Warzone (from Nov 6)
items.detail: Battle Royale gets Hajin (Verdansk stays); Resurgence gets Zodiac (industrial South Korea, railway through the map). MW4 movement replaces omnimovement and Tac Sprint is default (no perk needed) per reports. MW4 weapons and progression carry over.

items.name: Movement training course
items.detail: A dedicated movement training experience ships with launch; it grades runs from C- to S. Use it to drill mantle-into-slide, supine slide and ledge hang before ranked-style play.

items.name: Respawn modes
items.detail: Team Deathmatch, Domination, Hardpoint, Kill Confirmed and Free-for-All, each also in Hardcore.

items.name: New respawn modes
items.detail: Counter Attack, Inflation (cash drops; richest team wins) and Hijack.

items.name: Round-based
items.detail: Search & Destroy, Gunfight (2v2) and Gunfight 10v10.

items.name: Ground War
items.detail: 32v32, including Combat Outpost.

items.name: Party
items.detail: Gun Game and Drop Zone; Shipment, Possession and Infected added in launch week.

items.name: DMZ
items.detail: Hajin Exclusion Zone; 20 squads of up to 3 players.

items.name: Campaign
items.detail: A joint Korean and US Marine squad in Seoul.

items.name: Inflation
items.detail: 6v6 respawn, new mode. Kills collect part of the victim's cash; dying drops part of yours. Passing the High Value Target cash threshold reveals you to the enemy team. Overtime in the final minutes applies bigger cash mu…. Score None (most cash at time). Time 10 minutes. Win: Protect rich carriers; Push hard during Overtime multipliers. Mistake: Dying while carrying lots of cash.

items.name: Hijack
items.detail: 6v6 rounds. Carry, throw or pass the Data Spike to the enemy Comm Station; a plant scores over time, plus a bonus if the upload completes. Lethal button throws the Spike; it resets if dropped too long or thrown out of b…. Score 300. Time 4 minutes per round. Win: Escort the carrier as a group; Set up a defense around the planted Spike. Mistake: Carrier going solo.

items.name: Collateral
items.detail: Two-site bomb mode with a Counter-Strike-style economy. Start with a pistol and $800; earn cash from kills, objectives and round wins; buy in the Buy Phase. No respawns, health regen or custom loadouts. Death loses gear…. Score First to 6 round wins. Time 2 minutes per round. Win: Manage economy: save after losses; Buy UAV and armor on full-buy rounds. Mistake: Full-buying on broke rounds.

items.name: Gunfight
items.detail: 2v2 single-life rounds; everyone gets the same random loadout, which changes every two rounds. If time runs out an Overtime Flag appears: capture it, or win on health advantage. Launch maps: Cafe, Library, NYC, Smuggler. Score First to 6 rounds. Time 50 seconds per round. Win: Use utility early; Play for the flag or health lead when time is low. Mistake: Splitting from your teammate.

items.name: Kill Block (Gunfight 3v3 / 10v10)
items.detail: Gunfight on the modular Kill Block arena (two End Slabs + a Central Slab, 500+ layouts). Single life, shared random loadouts; sides swap after round one; layout and loadout change every two rounds; Overtime Flag decides…. Score First to 6 rounds. Time 50 seconds per round. Win: Adapt after every layout change; Trade as a group. Mistake: Running last round's route on a new layout.

items.name: Shipment 24/7
items.detail: Shipment (tiny container map) added Oct 27 to the 6v6 rotation plus a dedicated Shipment 24/7 playlist where the map stays fixed and modes rotate. No Hardcore Shipment 24/7 in the week of Oct 27 (single source). Popular…. Score Per the rotating mode. Time Per the rotating mode. Win: Bring Battle Hardened vs flash spam; Grenade-heavy play. Mistake: Standing still in the open.

items.name: Hardcore playlists
items.detail: Hardcore variants of TDM, Domination, Hardpoint, Kill Confirmed, Free-for-All and Search & Destroy (no Hardcore for party modes). Limited HUD, friendly fire, reduced health and no health regeneration (values not publish…. Score Per the base mode. Time Per the base mode. Win: Play slow; one or two shots kill. Mistake: Friendly fire.

items.name: Possession (limited-time, Oct 29)
items.detail: Halloween party mode: eliminating an opponent lets you take over their position and loadout. Full rules not published at research time. Win: Read rules in game. Mistake: Assuming standard TDM flow.

items.name: Drop Zone / Counter Attack (missing at launch)
items.detail: Listed on the August reveal but absent from the Oct 23 launch lineup per GamerFuzion's read of the official list; one guide still lists Drop Zone as a party mode. Treat as unavailable until seen in game.

items.name: Cachette (core 6v6)
items.detail: France: hideout/wine warehouse and mechanic's garage by a rail terminal. Cobblestone streets, shipping containers, rooftops and tight interiors; many flanks and upper-floor routes. Key routes: Backlot, Central Containers, Front Gate; central rooftops lead to Armory and Lounge. Beta complaint: spawn traps for the side without A-side spawn.

items.name: Cachette Hardpoint order
items.detail: Murder Box -> Graffiti -> Central Containers -> Armory -> Garage (single source, GamesAtlas). [Unverified]

items.name: Coal (core 6v6)
items.detail: Remote former Soviet coal-processing plant. Areas: Central Quarry, Processing Plant, warehouses, conveyor routes, loading areas, upper industrial walkways, outer perimeter. The quarry is the contested crossroads: don't cross it in the open; use warehouse routes to rotate and check high walkways first.

items.name: Coal Hardpoint order
items.detail: Conveyor -> Garage -> Stockpiles -> Under Structure -> Sorting (GamesAtlas). [Unverified]

items.name: Lithium (core 6v6)
items.detail: Mexican lithium refinery in the Sierra mountains. Defined by mid-range sightlines (favors AR, LMG, marksman). Garage doors toggle with wall buttons; you can slide under partly shut doors. A camouflaged truck on the east road overlooks Runoff Area and Refinery. Ranked #1 beta map by one creator.

items.name: Lithium Hardpoint
items.detail: Six hills on a fixed rotation; longest rotation P3 -> P4 (east side to southwest), so leave P3 early (Rankkd). [Unverified]

items.name: Lotus (core 6v6)
items.detail: South Korean fishing village after an amphibious assault: fish market, hostel, boathouse, gardens, restaurant, residential blocks. Interiors (Restaurant, Hostel, Fish Market, Boathouse) suit SMG/shotgun; main street has longer lines. Boathouse pipe climbs to lower roof and 2nd floor overlooking Docks; you can swim (have a pistol).

items.name: Lotus Hardpoint order
items.detail: Fish Market 1F -> Hostel 1F -> Boathouse 1F -> Garden -> Restaurant -> Market (Squid Statue) (GamesAtlas). [Unverified]

items.name: Mumbai (core 6v6)
items.detail: India: fugitive's hideout in a crowded residential district with a Victorian market and a railway line through it. Not in beta; little layout guidance published yet. Expect dense housing (close range) cut by market/rail lanes. [Unverified]

items.name: Munition (core 6v6)
items.detail: North Korean military command site around a large ammunition depot: hangars, monitoring rooms, crane, water tower and a linked skybridge (likely a power position over the lanes). Six Hardpoint hills per Rankkd. [Unverified]

items.name: Nautical (core 6v6)
items.detail: Damaged South Korean ferry: burning decks, debris and exposed outer decks. Not in beta; no detailed lane/spawn guides found. Expect long exposed deck lanes and tight interior corridors. [Unverified]

items.name: Reactor U92 (core 6v6)
items.detail: South Korean nuclear reactor complex in meltdown. Big concave command room with arcing electrical damage (key control point in objective modes) and a boiling containment pool at the center. Players holding the central space punish uncleared crossings. Not in beta.

items.name: Rooftops (core 6v6)
items.detail: Snowy New York rooftop of Hotel Times West: greenhouse, mechanical platforms (fans), patio, laundry room, pigeon coop; exterior walkways wrap the roofline, so check flank access before settling. Mix of closed rooms and open space.

items.name: Rooftops Hardpoint
items.detail: Rankkd: 6 hills, P1 mid, P2 north-west, P3 east (P2->P3 crosses almost the whole roof), P4 south-mid (B site), P5 north-mid (by A), P6 south-east. GamesAtlas names: Laundry Room, Fans, Greenhouse, Center, Patio, Pigeon Coop (start point conflicts). [Unverified]

items.name: Sentry (core 6v6)
items.detail: Military base in whiteout conditions (North Korea per most sources; one says Russian). Command/control center, damaged barracks, maintenance garage, generator room, substation, dome. Whiteout limits long sightlines; thermal/Cold-Blooded matter more. Not in beta.

items.name: Sentry Hardpoint order
items.detail: Control Center -> Barracks -> Dome -> Driveway (white jeeps) -> Utility (fuel depot) (GamesAtlas). [Unverified]

items.name: Silkworm (core 6v6)
items.detail: Dense Seoul shopping district centered on a subway entrance. Grounded street fights with few vantage points; beginner-friendly. Main Street cars can be set ablaze with frags/launchers/LMG fire. Game Room favors CQB; watch the Convenience Store from behind the counter. Ranked #2 beta map by one creator.

items.name: Silkworm Hardpoint order
items.detail: Subway Entrance -> Apartment Alley -> Game Room -> Main Street (armored vehicles) -> Storefront Alley -> Convenience Store (GamesAtlas). [Unverified]

items.name: Transit 213 (core 6v6)
items.detail: Small, high-intensity bus depot/parking lot in western India packed with colored buses; smallest core map in beta, Shipment-like pace. Grenades decide fights; buses give cover but draw grenades, so don't linger at one bus after a fight. Community favorite.

items.name: Transit 213 Hardpoint
items.detail: Rankkd: 5 hills, P1 mid bus lot, P2 north-east, P3 west (B site), P4 south, P5 north; P4->P5 is the longest rotation. GamesAtlas names: Center Lot, Repair Shop, Dumpster, Apartments, Luggage. [Unverified]

items.name: Shipment (6v6, added Oct 27)
items.detail: Classic tiny container yard. Constant spawns, grenade spam, fastest weapon/camo XP. One guide mentions flanking lanes and a forklift chokepoint. Run fast-ADS SMG/shotgun, Fast Hands, Battle Hardened, Bomb Squad.

items.name: Kill Block (modular arena)
items.detail: Built from three 'Slabs' (two End Slabs + a Central Slab) combining into 500+ layouts, some inspired by Crash, Highrise and Shoot House; about Shoot House size. Hosts Gunfight 3v3 and 10v10. Layout changes every two rounds per official rules (other guides say every round/match).

items.name: Gunfight: Cafe
items.detail: Paris courtyard with a theater, magazine kiosk and a central fountain (center cover/Overtime Flag area). [Unverified]

items.name: Gunfight: Library
items.detail: Wood-paneled state library with bookshelves and a central walkway raised over both sides; the walkway is the high-ground control point. [Unverified]

items.name: Gunfight: NYC
items.detail: Wintry downtown at night with a stage, stands, equipment cases and vendor stalls.

items.name: Gunfight: Smuggler
items.detail: Rail yard with parked train cars (fight inside or climb ladders onto roofs), warehouses and open ends.

items.name: Ground War: Imjin Farmland
items.detail: Rural Korea: open fields, farms, waterways, roads and rail tracks; relatively flat with narrow roads and shortcuts. Long sightlines: vehicles and snipers dominate open fields.

items.name: Ground War: Wolves Stadium
items.detail: Urban Ground War map in Hajin centered on a large stadium; expect vertical fights and stadium interior control.

items.name: Ground War: Forest
items.detail: Wooded hillside between Imjin Farmland and Wolves Stadium. Not in beta; layout details unpublished. [Unverified]

items.name: DMZ: Hajin
items.detail: Large Korean DMZ map (also coming to Warzone BR Nov 6). Includes a nuclear power plant area in the north-east. Exfil zones shown on the Tac-Map with a door icon.

items.name: Warzone: Zodiac (Resurgence)
items.detail: Industrial South Korean facility crossed by a railway; first playable in MW4 Open Beta, visibility improved after beta. Joins Resurgence Nov 6.

items.name: Power positions and head glitches
items.detail: No reliable MW4-specific head-glitch or spawn guides were published by Oct 28, 2026. Known strong spots: Lithium east-road truck, Lotus Boathouse roof/2nd floor, Library center walkway, Munition skybridge, Reactor command room. Verify in game. [Unverified]

items.name: Map pool notes
items.detail: Six core maps were in the beta (Cachette, Lithium, Lotus, Rooftops, Silkworm, Transit 213); six debuted at launch (Coal, Mumbai, Munition, Nautical, Reactor U92, Sentry). Some counts say 20 or 21 MP maps depending on Shipment/Kill Block.

items.name: Main menu / sidebar
items.detail: MW4 uses a cleaner UI with vertical menus and a left-docked pop-out 'blade' sidebar giving quick access to modes and Create-a-Class in MP and DMZ. Faster loading than Black Ops 7 menus per early impressions.

items.name: Playlist / mode select
items.detail: Mode tiles for Core 6v6 (respawn and objective), Gunfight/Kill Block, Ground War, Party modes and Hardcore. Map voting was enabled during the beta and is expected in lobbies. [Unverified]

items.name: Create-a-Class / Loadout
items.detail: Unified loadout: operator, primary, secondary, lethal, tactical, field upgrade, 3 perks (one per slot) and the 3 killstreaks are all saved per loadout (first time in a Modern Warfare game). Create-a-Class unlocks at player level 4.

items.name: Gunsmith
items.detail: Up to 5 standard attachments plus a separate Apex slot (unlocked at max weapon level). Apex attachments may block some slots. Weapon level progress counts across MP, DMZ and Warzone. DMZ looted guns can have up to 8 attachment slots.

items.name: Prestige choice screen
items.detail: At level 55 you choose Classic prestige (reset unlocks, +20% XP, permanent unlock token) or Regular (keep unlocks). 10 prestiges then 1,000 Prestige Master levels. Weapon Prestige locks attachments and moves the gun to a classic level unlock path.

items.name: Pre-match lobby
items.detail: Shows map and mode, team rosters and (when on) map vote. Use it to swap loadouts for the map: AR/marksman for Lithium, SMG/shotgun for Transit 213, Shipment, Lotus interiors. [Unverified]

items.name: Scoreboard (in match)
items.detail: Opened by holding Options/Tab: team scores, each player's score, kills, deaths, assists and objective stats. Exact columns in MW4 not verified. [Unverified]

items.name: Death screen and killcam
items.detail: After death a killcam replays the killer's view (Skip Killcam setting exists; guides recommend leaving it on to learn enemy angles). Expect killer name, weapon and health remaining; exact panel contents not verified. Then respawn with the option to change loadout. [Unverified]

items.name: Final killcam / end of match
items.detail: Series standard: final killcam of the winning play, then top-players podium, XP and weapon-level progress, challenge/camo progress. MW4-specific layout not verified. [Unverified]

items.name: Tac-Map (DMZ)
items.detail: Full-screen map in DMZ showing objectives, contracts and exfil zones (door icon). Exfil call triggers a countdown timer on screen.

items.name: Collateral buy menu
items.detail: Between rounds in Collateral: buy weapons, armor, perks, equipment and team UAV with cash (start $800). One guide claims 26 options. [Unverified]

items.name: Kill Block round transition
items.detail: Kill Block shows the new Slab layout and shared loadout every two rounds; read the new layout before moving.

items.name: Movement course results
items.detail: Movement training course grades runs from C- to S.

items.name: Settings: Interface/HUD
items.detail: Options include HUD Bounds, minimap shape (square recommended) and rotation, compass on/off, stamina bar toggle, HUD widget shake, crosshair dot size, color filters (filter 2 commonly suggested), FPS/ping/packet-loss telemetry, killcam skip.

items.name: Settings: Movement
items.detail: Sprint Assist (single-tap run is default with Blood Rush), Mantle Assist, Grounded Mantle, slide/dive behaviour. Guides suggest Sprint Assist on with zero delay; auto Tac Sprint may slow ADS. [Unverified]

items.name: Main menu
items.detail: Campaign, Multiplayer and DMZ (layout unverified).

items.name: Map vote
items.detail: Map voting is back in multiplayer lobbies.

items.name: Create-a-Class
items.detail: Unlocks at level 4: primary, secondary, three perks (one per slot), lethal, tactical, field upgrade and up to three streaks.

items.name: Killcam
items.detail: After a death: replays the kill from the enemy's view and shows a kill card with their weapon.

items.name: Theater
items.detail: Theater mode is available to watch matches back.

items.name: Minimap
items.detail: Top-left corner (IW Modern Warfare convention). Shows teammates, UAV/radar pings and objectives. Recommended: square shape, rotation on. Birdseye perk zooms it out and shows enemy facing on pings. Counter UAV scrambles it. [Unverified]

items.name: Firing red dots
items.detail: Unconfirmed for MW4. MWII/Warzone 2 removed unsuppressed-fire red dots from minimap and compass; one MW4 DMZ settings guide implies red dots appear on the compass when enemies shoot. Verify in game before coaching around it. [Unverified]

items.name: Compass
items.detail: Top-center compass bar can be toggled on/off in Interface settings; recommended on. May show pings/markers. [Unverified]

items.name: Score and timer
items.detail: Team scores and match timer sit with the minimap at the top-left in IW Modern Warfare titles; objective status (A/B/C flags, Hardpoint timer, bomb) appears alongside. [Unverified]

items.name: Killfeed
items.detail: Left side of the screen above the chat (series convention): killer, weapon icon, victim; headshot icon. Use it to track who is alive in S&D/Gunfight. [Unverified]

items.name: Ammo, weapon and equipment
items.detail: Bottom-right: current weapon, mag/reserve ammo, lethal and tactical counts; field upgrade charge meter nearby. [Unverified]

items.name: Killstreak meter
items.detail: Shows the 3 selected killstreaks and progress (kills plus Smart Streak objective credit) near the lower right; ready streaks highlighted with the D-pad/number key prompt. [Unverified]

items.name: Objective markers
items.detail: World-space icons for flags (A/B/C), Hardpoint zone, Data Spike/Comm Station (Hijack), bombs (S&D/Collateral), dog tags (KC), cash HVT reveals (Inflation).

items.name: Hitmarkers and damage
items.detail: Hitmarkers at the crosshair (different for kills/armor), red directional damage arcs showing where you're being hit from. Track damage direction to find the shooter. [Unverified]

items.name: Stamina bar
items.detail: Tac Sprint/stamina indicator can be hidden in settings. Tac sprint slows as stamina drains.

items.name: HVT reveal (Inflation)
items.detail: Players carrying cash past the threshold are revealed to both teams on the HUD/minimap as high-value targets.

items.name: Smart Streak/feedback popups
items.detail: Score popups (+XP) for kills, captures, holding Hardpoint and planting the Data Spike; these objective actions also fill the streak meter.

items.name: High Alert pulse
items.detail: With High Alert equipped, the screen edge pulses toward an unseen enemy who is spotting you.

items.name: HUD clarity
items.detail: Reviewers describe the MW4 HUD as cleaner while showing the same info. HUD Bounds can pull elements toward screen center.

items.name: HUD bounds
items.detail: A setting moves HUD elements toward the centre; killfeed duration, compass and stamina bar are configurable.

items.name: Hipfire
items.detail: No hipfire bloom.

items.name: Attachment rules
items.detail: 5 standard Gunsmith attachments + 1 Apex slot that does not use a standard slot. Apex unlocks at max weapon level; 28 Apex attachments at launch (counts vary).

items.name: Attachment: suppressors (FSS Crackdown, XRK Herder 40, XRK Mil-Tac)
items.detail: Common on SMG/AR meta builds: keeps you off enemy radar when firing (if firing reveals you) and adds recoil/range control. [Unverified]

items.name: Attachment: barrels (ZLR Carbon-900, 18 LE Crosswind, SA H86 465MM)
items.detail: Range barrels: Carbon-900 extends ISO Nightshade effective range past ~15 m; 465MM is a pro HAN 86 pick.

items.name: Attachment: optics (Slimline Elite, ZLR Type C, SZ Prima-4)
items.detail: Slimline Elite mini reflex is the most common pro/meta optic on M4 and HAN 86.

items.name: Attachment: grips (Demo STP-1 rear, FSS Fireline, FSS TAC90, XRK Justice II)
items.detail: Demo STP-1 rear grip appears on most ISO Nightshade builds; Fireline/TAC90 for AR recoil control.

items.name: Attachment: stocks (PF1 Fixed, Demo Dozer, EXP G2-44, FR4 Retractable)
items.detail: Fixed stocks for AR recoil; retractable/light stocks for strafe and ADS speed.

items.name: Attachment: lasers and ammo (SA Laz-500, QFL-S4.5, Pulse-MW, 5.56 Overpressured)
items.detail: Lasers speed ADS/hipfire for SMGs; 5.56 NATO Overpressured ammo boosts M4 damage range.

items.name: Perk system
items.detail: Pick three: one perk from each of 3 slots, 6 options per slot (18 total). Six perks are available when Create-a-Class opens at level 4; Kill Chain unlocks last (~level 48).

items.name: Killstreak system
items.detail: 17 streaks, chosen per loadout. Cost tiers 4/6/8/10/12 kills at launch (beta was 3/5/7/9/11); official patch notes reportedly say UAV is 5 kills (4 with Hardline) - conflict. Smart Streak meter: objective actions add progress. Streaks reset on death. Hardline -1.

items.name: Attachment slot: optic
items.detail: Sights/scopes; changes zoom and ADS time. Slimline Elite mini reflex is the most common pro/meta optic. Many meta builds skip the optic for irons. Notable: Slimline Elite: pro staple on M4/HAN 86; SZ Prima-4 Dot: WZStats HAN/Striga/Cronen builds; SZ Micro D-3 / IOTA-D: APOC, Oris, Type 73, M4 Apex; Cronen R808: Mosin/Oris marksman scope

items.name: Attachment slot: muzzle
items.detail: Suppressors, comps and chokes. Suppressors reportedly keep you off enemy radar when firing [unverified]; comps reduce recoil. X-58 Nyx has an integral suppressor and no muzzle slot. Notable: FSS IS300: M4/HAN/Axion/Hyeon builds; XRK Herder 40: ISO/VEL suppressor; FTAC Silent Recon: PPSh/Striga; Corvus LVL-40: pro HAN comp

items.name: Attachment slot: barrel
items.detail: Changes damage range, velocity and handling. Range barrels extend falloff (one Nyx barrel lists range x1.25). Notable: ZLR Carbon-900: ISO range past ~15 m; SA H86 465MM: pro HAN 86, falloff ~32 m; HAN 86 Silenced 413MM: integral-suppressor barrel; Bryson Longhorn 20": Cronen

items.name: Attachment slot: underbarrel
items.detail: Foregrips for recoil and aim stability; Apex conversions can add underbarrel launchers (Volt, Ember, Breach). Notable: FSS Fireline Grip: M4/VEL/Patriot/Oden/Axion; FSS TAC90 Grip: HAN/ISO/Kastov/MAR-9; Bruen Renegade Grip: LMGs; Mire-50 Tac Grip: Nyx

items.name: Attachment slot: stock
items.detail: Recoil vs ADS/strafe speed trade-off. Fixed stocks steady ARs; light/retractable stocks speed handling. Mosin Pistol Stock: ADS ~250 ms but one-shot range ~37 -> ~19 m. Notable: PF1 Fixed: M4 recoil; ZLR ASP50: M4 WZStats; Meiko L9P-Fold: HAN; VEL 46 Extended

items.name: Attachment slot: laser
items.detail: Speeds ADS and sprint-to-fire, helps hipfire; matters more because MW4 removed hipfire bloom. On nearly every WZStats meta build. Notable: Schlager Visiv-5: most common meta laser; SA Laz-500: M4/Patriot/MAR-9; SZ Gen.6 PEQ: Cronen/APOC/Warlord; XRK Clutch-LS: Signal 50, Oden Sentinel

items.name: Attachment slot: ammo
items.detail: Ammo types change damage range, velocity or penetration. Frangible variants appear on many builds (exact MW4 effect not documented). Notable: 5.56 NATO Overpressured: boosts M4 damage range; 7.62 Tokarev Frangible: PPSh; 12.7x55mm High Velocity: Oden Sentinel; Armor Piercing: Astaroth penetration

items.name: Attachment slot: magazine
items.detail: Capacity vs handling. Some builds take a smaller mag for speed (PPSh 53, FiNN 75, Oris 6). Notable: 40-round mag: ISO Nightshade; 35 Round Mag: Striga; 30 Round Mag: Cronen (from 20); 60 Round Drum: HAN 86 (DMZ build)

items.name: Attachment slot: rear grip
items.detail: Recoil control and ADS/sprint-to-fire tuning. Notable: Demo STP-1: on most ISO builds; ZLR Phase Grip: M4; LM Combat Grip: VEL Apex; BOK-980: Nyx

items.name: Attachment slot: apex
items.detail: Free 6th slot unlocked at max weapon level; does not use one of the 5 standard slots. Many Apex attachments convert the gun (fire mode, ammo, underbarrel, dual-wield). Launchers and the knife have none. Some beta Apex return later (Oct 23 notes). Notable: M4 Hurricane: 50-rd 5.7x28mm top mag; HAN X20 Skybreaker: airburst GL + targeting optic; Hyeon Hyperburst / Hyeon Auto; Oden Sentinel: semi-aut…

items.name: Attachment slot: bolt
items.detail: Shotguns/marksman: action tuning for fire rate and handling. Notable: ZLR Competition-B6: Rezi 12; Lightfir-5 Quick Bolt: Oris 8.6

items.name: Attachment slot: comb
items.detail: Sniper/marksman cheek rest; aim stability and ADS. Notable: Haebang YNC-45: KG-7; KV-R98 Comb: Oden Sentinel

items.name: Attachment slot: trigger action
items.detail: Pistols: trigger tuning (fire rate/handling). Mojave Lawless Apex blocks it. Notable: P68 Tapper 9: Krait

items.name: Attachment slot: cylinder
items.detail: Mojave .357 only (official attachment list). Notable:

items.name: TTK overview
items.detail: Launch keeps the slower Beta Weekend 2 TTK after Weekend 1 complaints. Community numbers (beta/launch, approximate): AR ~280-300 ms close, ~370-460 ms at 40-80 m; top SMGs ~240-260 ms at 0-10 m. Numbers vary by site and patch.

items.name: No bloom: Ballistic Authority
items.detail: Hipfire bloom removed: bullets go where the barrel points. Recoil is input-tied with a 'jerk' layer for natural kick/sway. Hipfire is consistent, so close-range hipfire with lasers is viable.

items.name: Flinch and one-shot tuning
items.detail: Launch added more flinch and damage tuning to one-hit-kill weapons (snipers/marksman). Shoot snipers first to throw off their aim.

items.name: SMG range buff
items.detail: Launch buffed SMGs at close-to-mid range, so ARs should avoid tight corners and hold lanes.

items.name: Headshot multipliers
items.detail: Modest: M4 1.2x (cut from 1.5x in beta); HAN 86 cut to ~1.25x. Beta Weekend 2 reduced headshot multipliers across most classes. Coaching: Coach upper-chest consistency over head flicks; a missed head flick costs more than the small multiplier gains.

items.name: No omnimovement
items.detail: MW4 drops Black Ops 6/7 omnimovement (no sprint/dive in any direction). Movement is grounded: sprint, slide, mantle, ledge hang, climb, jump.

items.name: Tactical Sprint
items.detail: In MP, Tac Sprint requires the Blood Rush perk (Perk 2); single-tap run is the default input; no sprint-out penalty per launch notes. Tac sprint slows as stamina drains. In DMZ (and reportedly Warzone) it's default.

items.name: Sprint-to-fire
items.detail: Coming out of sprint/tac sprint delays your first shot; settle before a peek. Auto Tac Sprint may slow ADS. Exact sprint-to-fire ms not published. [Unverified]

items.name: Slides and slide cancel
items.detail: Sliding and slide-into-ADS remain; slide canceling is reported possible. New Supine Slide: double-tap crouch while sprinting for a longer, lower slide ending on your back, feet first.

items.name: Mantle system
items.detail: Mantle Momentum keeps forward speed; Mantle Steering lets you steer or abort mid-mantle; Mantle Slide chains a mantle into a slide (e.g. over a car or planter into a room).

items.name: Ledge hang and shimmy
items.detail: Ledge hangs return (faster than MWII) with shimmy. Use to peek over ledges and surprise defenders.

items.name: Footstep audio
items.detail: Beta Aug 22 and Aug 25 patches cut footstep/gear audible distance and volume; Aug 29 restored the previous maximum audible distance to match live Warzone. Final launch mix not documented. Ninja greatly reduces your audible range. Coaching: If the user was flanked silently, check whether the enemy ran Ninja or the user was making noise (sprinting) themselves. Recommend a headset and low music volu…

items.name: Smart Streak meter
items.detail: Kills feed the killstreak meter in all modes; objective actions also add progress (capturing/holding Domination flags, holding the Hardpoint, planting the Hijack Data Spike). Points per action are not published. A death breaks the chain (full reset implied, not stated). Coaching: In objective modes, praise captures and holds; they build streaks as well as score. Chasing kills off the objective is…

items.name: Killstreak costs
items.detail: 4/6/8/10/12 tiers (UAV possibly 5). Hardline -1. Kill Chain lets streak kills count (reportedly at half) toward further streaks. [Unverified]

items.name: Loadout rules
items.detail: Primary + secondary (Overkill for two primaries), 1 lethal, 1 tactical, 1 field upgrade, 3 perks (one per slot), 3 killstreaks per loadout. 5 attachments + Apex.

items.name: Weapon leveling and Apex
items.detail: Leveling a gun to max unlocks its Apex attachment; weapon XP is shared across MP, DMZ and Warzone. Shipment and Decoy Grenade tricks are popular for weapon XP.

items.name: Hardpoint rotation
items.detail: Zone moves every 60 s in a fixed per-map order; some maps have 5 hills, Lithium and Munition 6 (per Rankkd).

items.name: Domination spawns
items.detail: Holding flags influences spawns; triple-capping flips enemy spawns toward your back flag. Sides switch at half score (100).

items.name: Frontline spawns
items.detail: Fixed team bases; spawning is predictable, so fights happen in the middle. Kills outside enemy base score more.

items.name: Spawn logic generally
items.detail: MW4-specific spawn rules aren't documented. Beta complaints on Cachette (A-side spawn trap) and a Hijack spawn fix in the Oct 25 patch show spawns are still being tuned. [Unverified]

items.name: Launcher arming distance
items.detail: PILA missiles arm at ~11 m, RPG-8 at ~9 m; too-close shots won't explode.

items.name: UAV durability
items.detail: UAV health raised 100 -> 150 at launch: it takes more fire to shoot down; use launchers or SAM turret.

items.name: Garage doors (Lithium)
items.detail: Garage doors open/close with wall buttons; you can slide under a partly closed door.

items.name: Destructible/flammable cover
items.detail: Cars on Silkworm's Main Street can be set on fire with explosives/LMG fire; the Drill Charge bores through cover; Impact Warhead drills through floors.

items.name: Kill Block layout cycle
items.detail: Layout and shared loadout change every two rounds; sides swap after round one.

items.name: Collateral economy
items.detail: Start each half with a pistol and $800; earn cash from kills, objective actions and round wins; buy armor, perks, equipment, weapons and a team UAV in the Buy Phase. Death loses your loadout but keeps cash. No respawns, no health regen, no custom classes, only the team UAV as a streak. Coaching: Coach buys: don't full-buy after losses; save, then buy together. A lost round with good cash is bette…

items.name: Inflation economy
items.detail: Kills pick up part of the victim's cash; dying drops part of yours; passing a cash threshold reveals you as a High Value Target to the enemy team; Overtime in the last minutes applies bigger multipliers. Exact numbers not published. Coaching: A rich player dying is a bigger loss than a kill is a gain; tell HVT players to play safe near teammates.

items.name: DMZ exfil
items.detail: Call exfil at a smoke-marked zone (alerts nearby enemies), board and stay until the timer hits zero. Fulton balloons and Exfil Flares are alternates.

items.name: Movement in Warzone (Nov 6)
items.detail: Warzone switches to MW4 movement (no omnimovement); Tac Sprint is reportedly default there without a perk.

items.name: Movement
items.detail: Omnimovement and wall-jumping are removed; new supine slide, mantle slide, pipe climbing and hanging; slide-cancel stays. In the beta, tactical sprint moved into the Blood Rush perk (launch status unverified).

items.name: Smart Streaks
items.detail: Objective actions (captures, holding a Hardpoint, plants) add to the killstreak meter.

items.name: Perks
items.detail: Three perks, one from each slot of six.

items.name: Prestige
items.detail: Classic Prestige with 55 ranks, plus an alternative path that keeps your unlocks.

items.name: Movement: Sprint
items.detail: Default sprint for everyone. Coming out of any sprint delays your first shot (sprint-to-fire); exact ms not published. MW4 has no omnimovement: you sprint forward only, no sideways/backward sprint or 360 dives. Stop sprinting a step before a corner so your gun is up when you see the enemy Sprint between cover, walk or crouch-walk into contested space

items.name: Movement: Tactical Sprint (Blood Rush only)
items.detail: In MP, Tac Sprint exists only with the Blood Rush perk (Perk 2). With it, single-tap sprint goes straight into Tac Sprint (changeable in Movement Advanced Settings). Length is set by a stamina pool that refills over time; kills refill it. Launch removed the extra Tac Sprint sprint-out penalty. Use it for rotations, not for swinging corners Beta Aug 28 patch: Tac Sprint speed -4%, overall stamina…

items.name: Movement: Slide
items.detail: Crouch while sprinting to slide. Beta Aug 28 patch cut slide distance 10% and slide speed 9% and lengthened the slide-to-jump delay. Sliding into ADS is supported. Slide into a corner pre-aimed rather than sprinting into it Slide under partly closed garage doors on maps that have them

items.name: Movement: Slide cancel
items.detail: Reported as possible in MW4 but with a tighter timing window than older titles (reviewers call it more restrictive). Exact inputs and timing not published. Don't build your game around slide-cancel speed; it was deliberately nerfed in beta

items.name: Movement: Supine Slide
items.detail: Official: double-tap crouch during a sprint for a longer, lower slide that ends supine (on your back, feet forward). One guide says ADS takes longer out of it. Use it to slide under sightlines or surprise a held angle low Expect slower ADS; don't supine-slide into a fair 1v1

items.name: Movement: Mantle (Momentum + Steering)
items.detail: Official: Mantle Momentum keeps forward speed until you clear the obstacle; Mantle Steering lets you steer left/right mid-mantle, aim down sights, or abort the mantle after it starts. ADS during the mantle to peek over cover safely Abort if you see an enemy waiting on the other side

items.name: Movement: Mantle Slide
items.detail: Official: go straight from a mantle into a slide (e.g. over a car hood or low cover into a room). Great entry over low cover into objective rooms Pre-aim where you land

items.name: Movement: Ledge hang, shimmy and hang lean
items.detail: Hang from ledges and shimmy along edges and pipes. Players can lean while hanging; guides describe aiming and rotating while hanging (hang lean). Faster than MWII ledge hangs per earlier research. Hang below a rooftop edge and pop up behind defenders Listen for enemies hanging on ledges near objectives

items.name: Movement: Jump and jump-shot
items.detail: Standard jump. No MW4 data on jump-shot accuracy or penalties; no hipfire bloom exists, but sway and recoil still apply. Don't rely on jump-shots until tested; ground strafing is safer

items.name: Movement: Dive / dive-to-prone
items.detail: No dolphin dive or omni-dive confirmed in MW4. One fan wiki lists dive-to-prone; unverified. Treat dive as unavailable unless seen in the user's own footage

items.name: Movement: Lean and weapon mount
items.detail: Hang lean is the only lean confirmed by mainstream coverage. A fan wiki lists tactical weapon mounting and a Tactical Stance (canted aim); unverified for MW4. If mounting exists, mount on cover edges for recoil control when holding lanes

items.name: Movement: Crouch and prone
items.detail: Standard crouch and prone stances. No MW4-specific crouch speed data (one guide claims Blood Rush speeds crouching; unverified). Crouch at the edge of cover to show less of your body Prone is slow to get out of; avoid in close range

items.name: Movement: Movement settings
items.detail: Settings include Sprint Assist, Mantle Assist and Grounded Mantle, and slide behaviour; Tac Sprint behaviour with Blood Rush is set in Movement Advanced Settings (single-tap run default, double-tap options remain). Guides suggest Sprint Assist on with no delay, but auto Tac Sprint can slow ADS out of sprint (unverified)

items.name: Movement: Mobility Course
items.detail: Dedicated training mode with guided tutorials and timed courses (Standard and Expert). S rank is the top grade; Expert S unlocks a weapon charm (sub-56 s per one guide). Drill Mantle Slide, Supine Slide and ledge hangs here before applying them in matches

items.name: TTK model
items.detail: Launch keeps the slower Beta Weekend 2 TTK (weapon-by-weapon damage cuts rather than more health). Community numbers: M4 ~296 ms (0-10 m), ~335 ms (10-40 m), ~422 ms (40-80 m), ~489 ms (80-120 m). Top SMGs ~240-260 ms up close. Coaching: A ~300 ms TTK means the player who shoots first usually wins unless they miss; judge deaths on who saw whom first and whether the user was mid-sprint, reloading…

items.name: Range-band damage
items.detail: Damage steps down at fixed distance thresholds rather than decaying smoothly (e.g. M4 drop-off at ~26 m per Codmunity). SMGs were buffed at close-to-mid range at launch. Coaching: If the user lost a fight just past a gun's range band, point to the distance, not the aim. SMG users should not take 30 m+ fights vs ARs.

items.name: Flinch
items.detail: Weekend 2 increased flinch on marksman and sniper rifles when hit; launch added more flinch/damage tuning to one-hit-kill weapons. Coaching: Against snipers, shooting first throws their aim. When the user snipes and loses, check whether they were shot before they fired.

items.name: No hipfire bloom (Ballistic Authority)
items.detail: Bloom removed from hipfire: shots go where the barrel points. Recoil, convergence and handling rebuilt to reflect player input; sway, recoil and movement still affect accuracy. ADS bloom behaviour not documented. Coaching: Close-range hipfire with SMGs/shotguns is viable; a missed close hipfire is a tracking error, not RNG.

items.name: Health and regeneration
items.detail: Base MP health value not published (one secondary source claims 150 HP; unverified). Health regenerates after a delay (value unpublished); Quick Fix and Stim start regen instantly. No regen in Collateral and Hardcore. Coaching: After a fight, the user should reset (cover, Stim or Quick Fix) before re-peeking. Back-to-back fights on low health are a common death cause.

items.name: Armor
items.detail: No armor plates in core 6v6 MP. Armor exists as a buy option in Collateral (and in DMZ, out of scope). Argonaut is a heavy-armor killstreak. Coaching: Don't expect armor-break hitmarkers in core modes; in Collateral check whether the enemy bought armor before judging a lost duel.

items.name: Minimap and red dots
items.detail: Minimap in the top-left (IW convention). Whether unsuppressed fire shows a red dot in MW4 is unconfirmed (one low-reliability fan wiki says a dot appears for a few seconds). Coaching: Don't assume firing reveals the user; verify in the user's own footage whether red dots appear when enemies shoot.

items.name: UAV behaviour
items.detail: UAV costs 5 kills (4 with Hardline) per launch notes and has 150 HP (raised from 100). It shows enemy red dots on the team minimap; Birdseye adds facing arrows; Ghost hides from it. Advanced UAV shows facing in real time and can't be locked on. Coaching: When the enemy has a UAV up, the user must move and avoid predictable spots; when the user's team has one, they should push using the dots. Note…

items.name: Counter UAV
items.detail: Scrambles all enemy minimaps while active (6 kills). Coaching: If the user's minimap shows static, play by sound and callouts and expect a push.

items.name: Spawn logic
items.detail: Beta patches adjusted spawns across respawn modes to better separate players and greatly reduced spawning on squad members; IW called spawn placement unfinished. Oct 24-25 patches fixed Hijack spawn/respawn timing. Frontline gives a short spawn-invincibility window. Coaching: Spawn deaths may be the game's fault; judge whether the user stayed near a spawn they flipped. In Domination, triple-cappi…

items.name: Hitmarkers and kill alerts
items.detail: Audio setting 'Headshot & Kill Alerts' (default on). A hitmarker sound preset was a community request, not confirmed. Damage direction indicator not documented for MW4. Coaching: Use the hit and kill sounds to judge whether the user's shots landed. If no hitmarkers showed, it was an aim miss, not netcode.

items.name: Killstreak loadout rules
items.detail: 17 streaks; 3 equipped per loadout, saved in each Create-a-Class loadout. Cost tiers 4/6/8/10/12 at launch (beta was one lower). One source says the three must come from different cost tiers. Hardline -1. Kill Chain makes streak kills count at half. Nuke (30) is automatic. Coaching: Match streak picks to the user's typical streak length; a player averaging 4-5 kills a life should run UAV/Counter…

items.name: Perk system (Pick 3) and no Wildcards
items.detail: One perk from each of 3 slots, 6 per slot (18 total). No Wildcard system found in MW4; Overkill is a Perk 1 option. Six perks are available when Create-a-Class opens at level 4. Coaching: Suggest perk swaps by situation: Ghost vs UAV spam, Cold-Blooded vs AI streaks, Battle Hardened vs flash spam, Blood Rush for rotations.

items.name: Create-a-Class and loadouts
items.detail: Each loadout stores operator, primary, secondary, lethal, tactical, Field Upgrade, three perks and three killstreaks. Create-a-Class unlocks at level 4; one guide says up to 12 custom classes. Gunsmith: 5 attachments plus an Apex slot at max weapon level. Coaching: If the user swaps class mid-match, the streaks change with it; check that their streak meter targets still fit.

items.name: Equipment counters
items.detail: Bomb Squad (less non-streak explosive damage, fuse reset on pick-up, no knockdown); Trophy System (3 projectiles); Combat Grid (equipment and streaks through walls); DDOS (jams electronics); Battle Hardened (tacticals). Coaching: Repeated deaths to the same equipment type should trigger a specific perk/Field Upgrade swap suggestion.

items.name: Launcher arming
items.detail: PILA missiles arm at ~11 m and RPG-8 at ~9 m (from weapon research); point-blank shots don't explode. Coaching: A launcher shot at a close enemy that does nothing is an arming-distance error.

items.name: Aim assist and matchmaking
items.detail: IW tuned aim assist for Open Beta Weekend 2 and before launch and says it will keep monitoring. No SBMM change was announced. Crossplay lobbies mix controller and mouse players. Coaching: Don't blame aim assist for every lost duel; check positioning first.

items.name: Stamina posture cue
items.detail: One hands-on preview says remaining stamina is shown through the operator's weapon posture (lower gun = less stamina) during Tac Sprint; a stamina bar can also be toggled. Coaching: A vision model can read Tac Sprint use and depletion from weapon posture; the user arriving at a fight with no stamina means slow escapes.

items.name: S&D/Collateral XP and bomb bug
items.detail: Oct 25 patch raised kill XP in S&D and Collateral from 100 to 300 and rolled back a bomb-stretching fix (it broke bomb pickup in some spots); bomb stretching remains unfixed. Coaching: Odd-looking plants/defuses at range may be the known bug, not cheating.

items.name: Change 2026-08-24
items.detail: Open Beta patch: TTK nerfs on M4, HAN 86, Axion and others; HAN 86 full-damage range 26.1 -> 23.5 m, head multiplier 1.4 -> 1.25. Beta-era; launch retuned all weapons again.

items.name: Change 2026-09-28
items.detail: Infinity Ward: launch TTK close to Beta Weekend 2, SMGs buffed, ARs unchanged (second-hand, via DMZ Radar).

items.name: Change 2026-10-20
items.detail: Early Access update: no weapon balance changes; DMZ fix for the ISO Nightshade Apex not working as intended.

items.name: Change 2026-10-21
items.detail: Fixes: Rezi 12 showed 0.00 TTK in the Firing Range; Gunsmith attachment menu could stay on screen during deployment; Switch 2 players could not buy saved Blueprint changes.

items.name: Change 2026-10-23
items.detail: Patch notes say some beta attachments/Apex attachments will return in a later update.

items.name: Change 2026-10-25
items.detail: Update: S&D XP tripled, bomb fix rolled back, Hijack spawn fix. No weapon numbers; earlier research notes IW said more weapon tuning was being looked at.

items.name: Change 2026-10-27
items.detail: Shipment 24/7 added via weekly playlist update. No weapon balance changes or new weapons found.

items.name: Counter UAV spam
items.detail: Run Ghost (Perk 1). Shoot UAVs down with PILA/JOKR or SAM Airburst Turret (UAV now has 150 health). Your own Counter UAV scrambles their minimap. Move after every fight since you're shown on the minimap.

items.name: Counter ground AI streaks
items.detail: Wheelson and Railgun Sentry: Cold-Blooded hides you from AI targeting; destroy with launchers, DDOS, Shock Stick or Drill Charge; approach sentries from behind or from cover angles.

items.name: Counter air streaks
items.detail: Attack Heli, Deathstalker, Gunship: PILA (guided), JOKR (lock-on top attack) or SAM Airburst Turret; stay indoors; Cold-Blooded vs thermal/AI. Air Lockdown adds AA for their team, so wait it out.

items.name: Counter Argonaut
items.detail: Focus fire as a group, use explosives/launchers, keep distance from its cluster-grenade launcher, and trade rather than duel.

items.name: Counter recon equipment
items.detail: Ghost beats Portable Radar, Heartbeat Sensor and UAV; Cold-Blooded beats Snapshot Grenade, Recon Drone, thermals and High Alert; DDOS jams nearby sensors.

items.name: Counter tacticals
items.detail: Battle Hardened cuts Flash, Concussion and Screamer Mine effects (strengthened at launch).

items.name: Counter explosives
items.detail: Bomb Squad reduces non-streak explosive damage; Trophy System eats grenades on Hardpoint and bomb plants.

items.name: Hardpoint: how to win
items.detail: Rotate to the next hill ~10 s early, set up before the enemy, play off the zone rather than standing in the open, trade in pairs, use Quick Fix for regen on captures. Learn each map's fixed rotation (e.g. Transit 213 P4->P5 and Lithium P3->P4 are long).

items.name: Loadout archetype: SMG slayer
items.detail: ISO Nightshade or VEL 46 with laser/fast ADS; perks Quick Fix, Blood Rush (Tac Sprint), Battle Hardened. Best on Transit 213, Silkworm, Lotus, Shipment, Kill Block.

items.name: Loadout archetype: AR anchor
items.detail: M4 or HAN 86 with Slimline Elite, recoil grip/stock; perks Ghost or Quick Fix, Fast Hands or Bomb Squad, Cold-Blooded or Battle Hardened. Best on Lithium, Munition, Rooftops lanes.

items.name: Loadout archetype: sniper/marksman
items.detail: KG-7 Vulcan or Oris 8.6 with Overkill + SMG secondary. Hold long lanes (Lithium, Imjin Farmland); expect flinch tuning to punish getting hit first.

items.name: Loadout archetype: team support
items.detail: Ghost, Birdseye, Combat Grid with UAV/Counter UAV/Advanced UAV streaks and Portable Radar or SAM turret. Gives intel and shuts down enemy air.

items.name: Streak choice
items.detail: With the slower TTK, cheap streaks (UAV, Care Package, Counter UAV) and objective credit via Smart Streaks are more reachable; pick per-loadout streaks that fit the mode (Hardline + UAV/CUAV/Advanced UAV for objective play).

items.name: Map: Lithium
items.detail: Use AR/LMG/marksman for mid-range sightlines; take the east-road truck to watch Runoff and Refinery; use garage door slides for surprise entries.

items.name: Map: Lotus
items.detail: Pair a marksman rifle with an SMG (Overkill); shotgun/SMG for Restaurant, Hostel, Fish Market and Boathouse; climb the Boathouse pipe for the roof/2F angle over Docks.

items.name: Map: Transit 213
items.detail: Bring extra lethals; buses are grenade magnets, so move after each fight; SMG/shotgun dominate.

items.name: Map: Silkworm
items.detail: Street-level CQB map: fight in Game Room with CQB loadouts, hold the Convenience Store from behind the counter, ignite clustered cars on Main Street.

items.name: Map: Cachette
items.detail: Use rooftops and upper floors for flanks; avoid being pinned in the losing spawn - rotate through Backlot or Front Gate instead of the Central Containers choke.

items.name: Map: Reactor U92
items.detail: Control the command room in objective modes; don't cross the central space without clearing angles.

items.name: Map: Coal
items.detail: Don't cross the Central Quarry in the open; use warehouse routes for rotations and check upper walkways.

items.name: Using sound
items.detail: With footsteps retuned shorter, use a headset; Ninja for flanks; Tracker to follow footprints.

items.name: Info from the killfeed and killcam
items.detail: Watch killcams to learn enemy angles and spawn flow; use the killfeed in single-life modes to count remaining enemies.

items.name: Lanes and sightlines
items.detail: General Call of Duty map design (not checked per map): most core maps have three lanes; controlling the middle and avoiding long open sightlines with short-range weapons wins engagements.

items.name: Objective play
items.detail: Smart Streaks reward capturing and holding; objective modes are won by holding points, not kills alone.

items.name: Sprinting into fights
items.detail: Tac Sprint (Blood Rush) and sprint-out delay your first shot; enemies holding angles win. Slow down near corners.

items.name: Running Tac Sprint without Blood Rush expectations
items.detail: In MW4 MP Tac Sprint only exists with Blood Rush; players expecting BO6/7 omnimovement or default Tac Sprint misjudge rotations.

items.name: Ignoring UAVs
items.detail: Staying still while an enemy UAV is up; UAV now has 150 HP and many teams don't shoot it down. Run Ghost or shoot it down.

items.name: Using ARs in SMG territory
items.detail: Launch buffed SMGs at close-mid range; taking corner fights on Transit 213/Silkworm with a slow AR loses.

items.name: SMG lane fights
items.detail: ISO Nightshade falls off past ~15 m; don't challenge ARs/marksman on Lithium's long lanes.

items.name: Late Hardpoint rotations
items.detail: Arriving after the zone moves (60 s) means fighting set-up enemies. Rotate ~10 s early.

items.name: Triple-capping in Domination
items.detail: Flipping spawns and getting attacked from behind. Hold 2 flags unless you can lock the third.

items.name: Chasing kills in objective modes
items.detail: Not playing objectives wastes Smart Streak credit and loses the game; captures/holds fill your streak meter.

items.name: Standing next to buses on Transit 213
items.detail: Buses attract grenades; reposition after each fight.

items.name: Point-blank launcher shots
items.detail: PILA/RPG won't arm under ~11/~9 m.

items.name: Skipping killcams
items.detail: Killcams show the angle and position you died to; skipping removes free info.

items.name: Not adapting to Kill Block layouts
items.detail: Reusing last round's route after the layout changes every two rounds.

items.name: Hiding in high-floor rooms vs Impact Warhead
items.detail: Impact Warhead drills through floors; move away from the marked area.

items.name: Ignoring Battle Hardened vs flash/stun spam
items.detail: Flash, Concussion and Screamer Mine are common; Battle Hardened was buffed at launch.

items.name: Not using Hardline when farming UAVs
items.detail: Hardline drops the UAV cost by one; helpful for objective players stacking intel streaks.

items.name: Over-relying on headshots
items.detail: Headshot multipliers are modest (e.g. ~1.2-1.25x on HAN 86); center-mass consistency wins more fights. [Unverified]

items.name: Dying with cash in Inflation
items.detail: Overextending while carrying lots of cash drops it to enemies and reveals you as an HVT.

items.name: Calling exfil without cover (DMZ)
items.detail: Calling the helicopter alerts nearby players and AI; secure the area first and stay aboard until the timer ends.

items.name: Wasting Collateral cash
items.detail: Buying full kits on eco rounds and going broke; plan buys with the team.

items.name: Treating guides as gospel
items.detail: Many MW4 numbers (TTK, unlock levels, tiers) are beta-era and conflict between sites; verify in game after patches.

items.name: Dying in the same area repeatedly
items.detail: Visible as deaths clustering on one part of the minimap; change route or approach.

items.name: Reloading in the open
items.detail: Killcams show the player reloading without cover.

items.name: Fighting at the wrong range
items.detail: Kill cards show the player losing to weapons that suit that distance.

items.name: TTK
items.detail: Time to kill: ms from first shot to kill. MW4 kept the slower Beta Weekend 2 TTK.

items.name: Ballistic Authority
items.detail: MW4 gunplay system: no hipfire bloom; bullets go where the barrel points.

items.name: Apex attachment
items.detail: Special weapon conversion unlocked at max weapon level; separate from the 5 Gunsmith slots.

items.name: Gunsmith
items.detail: Weapon customization: up to 5 attachments plus Apex.

items.name: Smart Streak meter
items.detail: MW4 killstreak meter: kills plus objective actions add progress; resets on death.

items.name: Killstreak
items.detail: Reward earned by kills (and objective credit) without dying; 17 at launch, chosen per loadout.

items.name: Field Upgrade
items.detail: Rechargeable ability (e.g. DDOS, Trophy System, SAM Turret).

items.name: Lethal / Tactical
items.detail: Damage equipment (frag, C4) vs utility equipment (flash, smoke, snapshot).

items.name: Overkill
items.detail: Perk to carry two primaries.

items.name: Hardline
items.detail: Perk making streaks cost one less kill.

items.name: Blood Rush
items.detail: Perk that grants Tactical Sprint in MW4 MP.

items.name: Tac Sprint
items.detail: Tactical Sprint: faster sprint burst draining stamina; MP needs Blood Rush.

items.name: Supine Slide
items.detail: MW4 slide via double-tap crouch while sprinting; longer, lower, ends on your back.

items.name: Mantle Slide / Steering / Momentum
items.detail: MW4 mantle features: chain into slide, steer/abort mid-mantle, keep forward speed.

items.name: Ledge hang
items.detail: Hang from a ledge and shimmy; returns in MW4.

items.name: Omnimovement
items.detail: BO6/BO7 360-degree sprint/dive system; not in MW4.

items.name: Slab
items.detail: A modular section of Kill Block (End Slabs and a Central Slab).

items.name: Kill Block
items.detail: MW4's modular arena with 500+ layouts for Gunfight 3v3/10v10.

items.name: Overtime Flag
items.detail: Flag that spawns when a Gunfight round's timer expires; capture it to win the round.

items.name: Data Spike / Comm Station
items.detail: Hijack objective item and the enemy target where it's planted.

items.name: HVT
items.detail: High-value target; in Inflation, players carrying lots of cash are revealed.

items.name: Buy menu
items.detail: Collateral's between-round shop for weapons, armor, perks, equipment and team UAV.

items.name: Combat Outpost
items.detail: Ground War mode: capture/reinforce outposts for points, spawns and vehicle/UAV rewards.

items.name: Exfil
items.detail: Extraction from DMZ by helicopter, Fulton balloon or flare; required to keep gear.

items.name: MIA
items.detail: Missing In Action: DMZ operator status after dying before exfil.

items.name: Tac-Map
items.detail: Full-screen map in DMZ showing exfils and objectives.

items.name: Classic / Regular Prestige
items.detail: MW4 prestige choice: reset unlocks for +20% XP and a token, or keep everything.

items.name: Prestige Master
items.detail: 1,000 levels after the 10th prestige.

items.name: Weapon Prestige
items.detail: Resets a weapon's attachments to a classic level path for rewards.

items.name: Head glitch
items.detail: Cover that exposes only your head while you shoot; flush with Drill Charge or explosives.

items.name: Power position
items.detail: Elevated or central spot with strong sightlines (e.g. Lotus Boathouse roof, Library walkway).

items.name: Trade
items.detail: Killing the enemy who just killed your teammate before they reset.

items.name: Rotation (Hardpoint)
items.detail: Moving to the next hill before it activates.

items.name: Spawn flip
items.detail: When a team's spawns move to the opposite side, often after triple-capping in Domination.

items.name: Flinch
items.detail: Aim kick when you're shot; increased on one-shot weapons at launch.

items.name: Hipfire
items.detail: Shooting without aiming down sights; consistent in MW4 because there's no bloom.

items.name: ADS
items.detail: Aim down sights.

items.name: CDL
items.detail: Call of Duty League; 2027 season plays on MW4.

items.name: GA
items.detail: Gentlemen's Agreement: competitive restrictions on items/perks; MW4 list not yet found.

playbook.title: Fight from cover
playbook.principle: Start every gunfight with most of your body behind something solid and a way out. Before each move, know where your next cover is if you get shot.
good: Shooting from a wall edge or doorframe
Crossing open ground only at full speed
Knowing your fallback spot
bad: Standing in the middle of a street or courtyard
Taking a fight with no cover in reach
signals: Killcam: your whole body visible, nothing between you and the killer
playbook.fix: Take fights only from the edge of cover you can step back behind.

playbook.drill: Private match: walk each map and name the next cover from every lane.

playbook.title: Cross sightlines quickly, and rarely
playbook.principle: Long lanes are where held angles live. Cross them at the narrowest point, at full speed, ideally while your team draws attention or smoke covers you.
good: Sprinting or sliding across the narrowest gap
Crossing right after a teammate fires
Using different crossings
bad: Walking or aiming down sights across an open lane
Stopping mid-lane
The same crossing every life
signals: Killcam: long-range kill, you mid-lane side-on, the killer still
playbook.fix: Cross lanes fast at the narrowest point, or take a route that avoids the lane.

playbook.title: Know whether you are holding or pushing
playbook.principle: A player holding a pre-aimed angle usually beats the player walking into it. Hold an angle the enemy must cross, or push only with information, numbers, utility or timing on your side.
good: Holding a lane the enemy must use
Pushing right after a kill, a trade or a UAV
Utility thrown before the push
bad: Walking into a held angle with no information
Holding an angle nobody needs to cross
signals: Killcam: the killer stationary and already aimed where you appeared
playbook.fix: Push only with information, a numbers advantage or utility; otherwise hold.

playbook.title: Use head glitches and high ground; avoid fighting into them
playbook.principle: Cover that hides your body but lets you shoot over it, or a higher position, makes you a much smaller target. Challenging those spots head-on from low, open ground is a losing trade.
good: Ledges, boxes and sills that show only your head
Making enemies look up at you
bad: Standing in the open below someone who shows only their head
Re-challenging the same head glitch
signals: Killcam: the killer looks down at you, or only their head and gun clear the cover
playbook.fix: Do not fight into a head glitch from the open: flank it, throw utility, or take another route.

sources.title: What is a head glitch, GameFAQs

playbook.title: Do not peek the same angle twice the same way
playbook.principle: After a failed or spotted peek, the enemy pre-aims that spot. Change position, height or timing, or reset.
good: Wide swing, crouch peek or a different door after a failed peek
One quick look per peek
bad: Re-peeking the same edge at the same height within seconds
Dying twice to the same player at the same spot
signals: Two deaths in a row to the same killer at the same spot
playbook.fix: After one peek, change the angle, height or timing, or leave.
