playbook.title: Move after you get a kill
playbook.principle: A kill gives away your position: a red dot if you are unsuppressed, plus a killcam for the player you killed. The next enemy comes to that spot.
good: Stepping back or shifting a few metres after the kill
Reloading behind cover
Pre-aiming where the next enemy will swing from
bad: Staying on the same angle and dying to the teammate of the player you killed
signals: Dying a few seconds after your own kill, at the same spot
playbook.fix: After every kill, move, reload in cover, then aim at the next likely entrance.

playbook.title: Play within trading distance
playbook.principle: Stay close enough that a teammate can kill your killer straight away, but far enough apart that one spray or grenade does not get you both.
good: A teammate covering your angle a few seconds behind
Trading kills
Never the lone player on a flank
bad: Far from every friendly dot
Stacked on a teammate and both killed together
signals: Death screen: no friendly dots near you on the minimap
playbook.fix: Stay one short sprint from a teammate who covers a different angle.

playbook.title: Do not sprint into likely contact
playbook.principle: After sprinting there is a delay before you can fire, longer after tactical sprint. A pre-aimed enemy wins that window, so slow down near corners and doorways with your gun up.
good: Releasing sprint before corners and doorways
Entering with the gun already up
bad: Rounding corners at full tactical sprint
Dying before the gun comes up
signals: Killcam: your gun lowered in a sprint pose when the first shot lands
playbook.fix: Stop sprinting before any corner or doorway that could hold an enemy.

sources.title: MW4 day-one habits, Techyorker
Sprinting vs ADS timing, MitchCactus

playbook.title: Reload behind cover, not in the open
playbook.principle: A magazine usually holds more than one kill, so reloading after every burst wastes your safest moments. Reload when you are out of sight.
good: Checking ammo, stepping behind cover, then reloading
Switching to the sidearm if caught empty
bad: Reloading in the open right after a kill
A reload interrupted by the next enemy
signals: Killcam or HUD: reload animation or an empty magazine at the moment of death
playbook.fix: Reload only behind cover, or finish the fight with your pistol.

Gunfight tips, TechRadar

playbook.title: Pre-aim common angles at head height
playbook.principle: Keep your crosshair where enemies will appear, at head height, so a fight needs only a small correction. Scump teaches this as centering.
good: Crosshair leading around corners at head height
Clearing one angle at a time
bad: Crosshair on the floor or a wall when you round a corner
Late flicks
signals: Killcam: you aimed away from where the killer appeared and turned only after being hit
playbook.fix: Before every corner, put your crosshair at head height where the enemy would appear.

playbook.drill: Private match: walk each map pre-aiming every doorway.

playbook.title: Peek cheaply for information
playbook.principle: When you do not know if an angle is held, use a short jiggle, a mantle you can abort, or a quick slide peek before you commit. MW4 lets you steer and abort mantles.
good: A quick jiggle, then a committed swing
Aborting a mantle when you see an enemy
Utility before the peek
bad: A slow, wide peek into a held angle
Committing to a full mantle in the open
signals: Killcam: you died mid-mantle or during a slow, wide strafe into a lane
playbook.fix: Jiggle or abort the mantle to get information, then commit once you know.

playbook.title: Read the minimap every few seconds
playbook.principle: In MW4, red dots show when an enemy fires an unsuppressed weapon or your UAV is up. Firing unsuppressed puts you on their minimap too.
good: Glancing at the map every few seconds
Moving toward red dots from an unexpected angle
A suppressor when you want to stay hidden
bad: Dying to an enemy who showed as a dot seconds earlier
Firing unsuppressed from one spot and getting flanked
signals: Death screen: a red dot near the killer before you died
playbook.fix: Check the minimap before every corner and face red dots before they reach you.

playbook.title: Play around UAVs
playbook.principle: With your UAV up, push with the information. With theirs up, assume you are seen unless you run Ghost, so stay near teammates and cover.
good: Pushing the moment your UAV goes up
Playing near teammates under an enemy UAV
Shooting it down
bad: Holding a lonely flank under an enemy UAV without Ghost
signals: An enemy UAV shortly before death, killer from behind or the side
playbook.fix: Under an enemy UAV, stay near teammates and cover or run Ghost; under yours, push.

playbook.title: Know where they will spawn
playbook.principle: Spawns depend on where both teams are. Pushing too deep, spreading out or wiping the enemy can flip spawns behind you.
good: Knowing the current enemy spawn
Holding angles that face it
Expecting a flip after a big push
bad: Chasing deep into their side
Getting shot in the back by freshly spawned enemies
signals: Killcam: the killer behind you, on the side your team held, early in their life
playbook.fix: After a wipe or a deep push, turn around, regroup and expect the spawns to flip.

playbook.title: Take power positions as a team
playbook.principle: Rambo: Call of Duty is a game of positional warfare. Positions that see the most lanes and the enemy spawn exits create favourable fights.
good: Overlapping lanes toward the enemy spawn
A power spot held with a teammate
bad: Alone in a power spot with no trade
Leaving a power spot to chase kills
signals: Killcam: crossfire from two directions on a spot your team held
playbook.fix: Learn two or three power positions per map and take them with a teammate.

playbook.title: Fight at your weapon's range
playbook.principle: SMGs and shotguns win close, assault rifles win mid range, snipers and marksman rifles win long. Damage drops with distance, so fights outside your range are uphill.

Assault rifle holding mid lanes

A long gun in a cramped room against a shotgun

playbook.title: Shoot first, be ready first
playbook.principle: Whoever lands the first shot usually wins. Arriving pre-aimed, gun up and not sprinting decides most duels.

Pre-aimed and firing on sight
bad: Reacting to being shot
Taking damage before your first shot

playbook.title: Hipfire close, aim at range, strafe

Aiming before peeking a mid lane
Strafing while firing
bad: Aiming down sights at point blank and losing the race
Standing still while aimed in a long lane
signals: Killcam: you scoped in at point blank, or stood still while the killer strafed

bad: Re-peeking at low health

strengths: Punish players camping roofs or upper floors
Clear an indoor Hardpoint/flag

Don't stack teammates in one building

strengths: Deny an objective or a choke for several seconds
Break a team holding a Hardpoint

Move away from it immediately

Clear a long lane full of enemies

Leave the marked line

Rely on audio and callouts while jammed

Hunt campers in corners

Shock Stick
DDOS
Cold-Blooded vs AI targeting

counters: Stay under cover and move between buildings
Cold-Blooded (unconfirmed)
tips: Lock enemies standing on flags/hills first
arsenal.look: User: aerial targeting view with lock-on boxes. Victims: missiles falling from above.

Approach from behind/outside its view
Launchers
Drill Charge

counters: PILA (guided), JOKR (lock-on top attack), SAM Airburst Turret
Cold-Blooded
Stay indoors

Objective modes late game

DDOS-type jamming
Play indoors and keep moving

arsenal.summary: Player-controlled helicopter with twin turrets that overheat.
strengths: Clear outdoor enemies and objectives from the air
counters: Launchers and SAM turret
Fight from cover while it overheats
tips: Burst-fire to manage turret heat
arsenal.look: User: helicopter gunner view with twin turret reticles and a heat meter. Victims: helicopter hovering and firing in bursts.

arsenal.name: Argonaut
arsenal.summary: Juggernaut-style heavy assault armor with a pump-action cluster grenade launcher and a burst-fire sidearm.

Launchers and explosives
Keep distance from the cluster launcher

Stay under hard cover

maps.name: Cachette
maps.setting: France. On the edge of a rail terminal, an abandoned wine warehouse and a derelict mechanic's garage now hide a covert armoury. Cobblestone streets, shipping containers, rooftops and small interiors (official).
maps.layout: Tall north-south map, north up on the Tac-Map. The north end is an open lot with parked cars beside the rail platforms. A diagonal cobblestone yard with stacked containers runs through the middle from north-west to south-east. Multi-storey blocks line the west and east sides. The Armory and Lounge sit upstairs beside the middle, and you reach them by hopping across container tops and low roofs. The south end splits into a south-west courtyard and a south-east block with the Garage. Official route names: Backlot, Central Containers and Front Gate.

callouts.name: Central Containers
callouts.look: Stacked shipping containers in an open cobblestone yard; you can jump across container tops and low roofs.
callouts.use: Mid lane and Hardpoint hill. Container/roof hops reach Armory and Lounge upper floors (official tip). Exposed from both building blocks.

callouts.name: Courtyard
callouts.look: Open central cobblestone yard around the containers.
callouts.use: mw4stats: avoid fighting over the open central yard; cross with smoke or via upper floors.

callouts.name: Armory
callouts.look: Upstairs hidden armoury with weapon racks. A DMZ-style 3D printer sits here; break it open and it drops a random weapon build (Reddit find reported by GameSpot).
callouts.use: Second-storey room reached from mid container/roof hops (official). Strong upper-floor angle over mid. HP hill #4 (GamesAtlas).

callouts.name: Lounge
callouts.look: Upper-floor lounge room next to the middle (furniture, interior).
callouts.use: Official tip pairs it with Armory as a second-storey advantage reached from the middle roofs.

callouts.name: Front Gate
callouts.look: Street/gate entrance; north lot with parked cars on the tac-map.
callouts.use: One of three official killstreak-target routes (Backlot, Central Containers, Front Gate).

callouts.name: Platform
callouts.look: Rail-terminal platform edge (long straight platform lines on the north boundary of the tac-map).
callouts.use: Community name (mw4stats; mw4.buzz's sheet runs 'Wine Cellar to Rail Yard'). A long open lane, so pre-aim from cover.

callouts.name: Backlot
callouts.look: Rear lot behind the buildings.
callouts.use: Official route name; expect flankers and killstreak traffic here.

callouts.name: Garage
callouts.look: Mechanic's garage: car inside, tools, roll-up doors.
callouts.use: HP hill #5 (GamesAtlas); close range - Zip Gun/SMG (cod-mw4.wiki). Take it early with the wine-cellar stairwell (mw4stats).

callouts.name: Wine Cellar
callouts.look: Wine warehouse cellar: barrels, racks, stone stairwell.
callouts.use: Community name (mw4stats, mw4.buzz). Take the cellar stairwell early with the Garage.

callouts.name: Graffiti
callouts.look: Graffiti-covered wall area.
callouts.use: Hardpoint hill 2 (GamesAtlas). RankKD puts P2 on the west side.

callouts.name: Murder Box
callouts.look: Enclosed space overlooked from several sides (name implies a killbox).
callouts.use: Hardpoint hill 1 (GamesAtlas). Hold it from outside, not from the middle of the box.

callouts.name: Mid Rooftops
callouts.look: Low flat roofs next to the central containers, joined by short jumps.
callouts.use: Descriptive label for the official tip's 'rooftops in the middle'. The roof route leads into the Armory and Lounge and gives a wider view of the yard.

callouts.name: Server Room
callouts.look: Small room with server racks (official name; its spot on the map is not published).
callouts.use: The official guide names it with the Garage and Armory as tight interior spaces. Bring a close-range gun or the Zip Gun lethal.

powerPositions.why: Second-storey view over the central yard and containers; official tip calls the upper routes a key advantage.
powerPositions.counter: Throw utility through the windows, then climb the container/roof route or push the stairs while a teammate holds the window.

powerPositions.why: Upper-floor angle onto mid next to Armory.
powerPositions.counter: Same as Armory: flash/stun and take the roof hop; do not peek it from the open yard.

powerPositions.why: Height over the yard and a fast route into both upstairs rooms.
powerPositions.counter: Hold the roof edge from the Armory window, or frag the roof before you cross the yard.

sightlines.why: [inferred from tac-map] Open north lot looks down the diagonal yard into mid.
Upper floor overlooks the open cobblestone yard.
Inferred: straight platform lines along the north edge.

maps.spawns: Not published. Beta feedback (Timesaver): the team without the A-side spawn could get trapped until spawns flipped. The tall layout suggests north and south starts, but this is not confirmed. The launch notes say spawns were adjusted on every map.

objectives.other: HP order from GamesAtlas (single source). RankKD: 5 hills, longest move P2->P3 (west side -> south end); P5->P1 is a short hop so you can stay longer. Dom/S&D positions not published. Five hills, 60 s each (GamesAtlas names; RankKD agrees on five). RankKD: the longest move is P2 to P3, west side to the south end. GamesAtlas names P3 Central Containers, which sits mid on the Tac-Map, so one of the two is off. Bomb sites and flags are not published.

modeTips.tdm: Fight from the upper floors around the middle. Do not stand in the open yard. Use the container hops to change height in a fight.
modeTips.domination: Spawn traps happen here. If you are pinned, break out through a flank route, not the main lane. Hold your flag and the upstairs rooms by the middle.
modeTips.hardpoint: Send a player early on the P2 to P3 move. P5 to P1 is short, so you can stay on the Garage longer. Hold the Armory and Lounge windows to cover Central Containers.
modeTips.sd: Sites are not published. Use the upper floors for information and smoke the yard before you cross.
modeTips.hijack: Carry the Spike through covered routes and the upper floors. The open yard is where carriers get caught.

maps.weaponFit: SMG or shotgun for the Garage, Armory, Server Room and other interiors (the official tip adds the Zip Gun lethal). AR for the yard and north lot. Explosive streaks on Backlot, Central Containers and Front Gate (official tip).

Ignoring the second-storey routes
Staying pinned in spawn instead of using flanks when spawns don't flip
Crossing the open yard without smoke
Staying pinned in spawn instead of using a flank when spawns do not flip

maps.name: Coal
maps.setting: Remote mountains in Russia. The remains of an old Soviet coal processing plant: a fallen smokestack, ore chutes and processing buildings that feed a slurry-filled river and a polluted flood plain (official).
maps.layout: Tall north-south map, north up. An open quarry fills the north and centre, with scattered machinery. A large processing complex sits on the north-east side. An enclosed east-west conveyor gallery cuts across the middle, and a second raised structure crosses the south. Warehouses and walkways give covered rotations around the quarry. Layout is read from the official Tac-Map and the u4gm guide.

callouts.use: Contested crossroads with the longest sightlines (u4gm). Do not cross in the open; check the high walkways first.

callouts.name: Processing Plant

callouts.use: Interior fights; covered route around the quarry.

callouts.use: mw4stats: pipe runs in the main hall are the best SMG flank route.

callouts.use: Hardpoint hill 2 (GamesAtlas). RankKD puts P2 on the east side.

callouts.use: HP hill #5 (GamesAtlas).

callouts.look: Warehouse sections with stacked materials.
callouts.use: Safer covered rotation routes around the quarry (u4gm).

callouts.look: Elevated industrial catwalks/platforms above routes.
callouts.use: Views over major routes but exposed if you linger (u4gm).

callouts.name: Ore Chutes
callouts.look: Tall angled chutes on the plant buildings.
callouts.use: Official feature. One guide says the map rewards control of the high ground along the ore chutes. Spot not mapped.

callouts.look: A toppled brick chimney lying across the ground.
callouts.use: Official landmark, useful as a callout anchor. Its spot on the Tac-Map is not confirmed here.

callouts.name: Loading Areas
callouts.look: Loading bays with ramps and parked plant equipment.
callouts.use: Named area in the u4gm guide. Close fights near the processing buildings.

callouts.look: Edge paths around the plant.
callouts.use: Named area in the u4gm guide. Flank routes away from the quarry.

powerPositions.why: Elevated views over the quarry and main routes (u4gm).
powerPositions.counter: Pre-aim/utility the walkways before entering the quarry; punish players who linger up there.

powerPositions.why: Covered cross-map gallery that lets one player hold both sides of the middle.
powerPositions.counter: Flash the gallery ends; flank through the Main Hall pipe runs.

powerPositions.why: One guide says the high ground along the ore chutes controls the map.
powerPositions.counter: Use smoke and push from below with two players at once.

sightlines.why: Longest lines on the map are across the open quarry.
[inferred] Plant edge overlooks the quarry floor.

maps.spawns: Not published. The tall layout suggests north and south starts, but this is not confirmed.

objectives.other: HP names GamesAtlas (single source). RankKD: 5 hills; longest move P2->P3, east side -> west side. One source calls Coal a good S&D map (careful, round-based play). Five hills (GamesAtlas names; RankKD agrees on five). RankKD: the longest move is P2 to P3, east side to west side. Bomb sites and flags are not published.

modeTips.tdm: Hold mid to long lanes from cover at the quarry edge. Do not sprint across the open pit.
modeTips.domination: Rotate through the warehouses and the conveyor, not across the quarry.
modeTips.hardpoint: Leave the Garage early: P2 to P3 crosses the whole map from east to west. Control the routes around a hill rather than stacking on it (u4gm).
modeTips.sd: Slow, information-first rounds. Clear the walkways before you cross the quarry. Long outdoor lanes punish rushed opening pushes (u4gm).
modeTips.hijack: Escort the Spike through the conveyor and warehouses. A carrier in the open quarry is easy to stop.

maps.name: Lithium

maps.name: Imjin Farmland
maps.setting: A low floodplain on Hajin's south-west edge: exposed rice fields, winding waterways, scattered farms, narrow roads and rail lines meeting at a vast industrial rice mill on high ground (official Hajin text). Cut from the DMZ map.
maps.layout: Flat farmland with narrow roads and shortcuts (official). A river runs on the west and south-west, and a rail bridge crosses the south. Farm buildings cluster north-west of centre. The rice mill complex with its warehouses sits east of centre on high ground, with storage tanks to the south-east. Read from the community overhead layout.

callouts.use: Official tip: the mill towers over the map and suits snipers. Approach from the outskirts in cover, breach the inner facility from several angles, then switch to close range. DMZ rates it Medium threat.

maps.name: Wolves Stadium
maps.setting: A dense district of Hajin City round a baseball stadium: multi-storey buildings, transit lines, tunnels, rooftops and hillsides (official). North of the stadium is a deserted open-air theatre; streets hold a police station, a bank, courtyards, small malls and apartments (official Hajin text).

maps.name: Hajin
maps.setting: A Korean exclusion zone: villages, farmland, a prison, an air base, a nuclear reactor and Hajin City (mall, wharf, stadium and the fortified Grid). 13 major POIs rated Low to Extreme threat for AI only (official Deep Dive).
maps.layout: Tac-Map grid A-J by 1-9, north up. The rural north-west holds the prison and border villages, with the air base and Deadtown down the west. Imjin Farmland is south-west. The middle has Cheongun Village, the hospital and the Cheonwang Peak Array. Hajin City fills the east and south-east: NuriGO Mall, The Grid, Songdo Wharf, Wolves Stadium and River Heights. The reactor is east, on the coast. Expressway No. 1 crosses east to west; the river runs from a north delta to a South Fork.

callouts.use: Major POI. Tac-Map square C3. Threat (AI only): Prison High; Prison Yard High; The Citadel Critical.

callouts.look: Air base cut into a granite hillside over a huge underground bunker, with cliffs, a toxic pool and missile bunkers nearby.

callouts.use: Major POI. Tac-Map square C7. Threat (AI only): Exterior Low; Re-Education Center Medium.

callouts.name: Imjin Farmland
callouts.look: Low floodplain of rice fields, waterways, farms and rail lines meeting at a huge rice mill.
callouts.use: Major POI. Tac-Map square D7. Threat (AI only): Exterior Low; Jeong Loading Dock Low; Rice Mill Medium.

callouts.name: Cheongun Village
callouts.look: Border village on the Hajin River with a casino; the Expressway runs along its south edge.
callouts.use: Major POI. Tac-Map square F4. Threat (AI only): Village Low; Outskirts Low; Russian Border Crossing Low; Heavenly Luck Casino High.

maps.spawns: Squads insert round the map. Exfil sites switch on from a pool each match and show green smoke: call the helicopter and hold the site until it lands; calling it alerts players and AI nearby. Fulton balloons and exfil flares also exist. Reported exfils: Songdo Pier, Cheongun Outskirts gas station, a River Heights roundabout, beside Deadtown.

objectives.other: Threat levels count AI only; a Low POI can still hold a squad. Grid cells conflict between fan maps (e.g. reactor H4/I4 vs G4). Threat levels count AI only; a Low POI can still hold a squad. Compounds hold better loot and intel. UAV towers ping nearby players; Lieutenant towers locate a Lieutenant. Radiation gear and a gas mask are needed at the reactor.

maps.name: Zodiac
maps.setting: Industrial South Korean weapons and drone factory on a compact island, crossed by a railway with several trains. Features: moving solar panels, furnace conveyor belts, signs that warn of incoming trains, and a burning Admin Tower used for sniper fights (official beta notes).
maps.layout: Ten named POIs round a central double rail line (Trackline). High ground runs along the north (Admin, Solar, Old Mines), the main industrial complex fills the middle, and the shoreline is to the south (Cooling, Sentinel). Trackline has rooftops, high windows and tunnels for rotations. Rough positions come from guides and a teaser image.

limitations: Frames are sampled every 2–3 seconds, so fast deaths and kills can be missed; deaths are mostly caught on the killcam or death screen.
Death areas need a visible, fixed minimap; they are approximate.
Map, weapon and perk lists come from launch-week research; check them after patches.
Live tips only in the campaign and private matches with bots; everything online is reviewed after the match.

Fight details (cover, movement, range, height, support) are read from the killcam, which is a reconstruction and can be slightly off; findings are probable, not certain, and untagged deaths are counted, never guessed.
Kills are tagged only with what the player's own view shows (range, movement, height).
